title: COCA High-Yield Collocations
subtitle: Natural Spoken Register & Authentic Idiomatic Stems
citation: Mark Davies (2008-). The Corpus of Contemporary American English (COCA): One billion words, 1990-present. Brigham Young University.
description: Drawn directly from COCA's 1-billion-word balanced American corpus. Filtered for high Mutual Information (MI) scores in spoken registers to cultivate authentic, idiomatic communicative competence.

words.definition: The quality of being open to more than one interpretation; inexactness in communication.
words.example: Clear, explicit documentation eliminates ambiguity in distributed software engineering teams.

words.definition: The action or state of forming a united whole; logical, unified flow in discourse.
words.example: Effective expository writing requires tight paragraph cohesion and clear conceptual transitions.

words.definition: A person or thing holding a corresponding position or function in a different organization.
words.example: The lead product manager met regularly with her engineering counterpart to align sprint goals.

words.definition: The process or state of drawing apart or becoming distinctly different in trend or opinion.
words.example: The quarterly financial report highlighted a sharp divergence between revenue and actual operating margins.

words.definition: A likely consequence or conclusion that can be drawn although not explicitly stated.
words.example: The decision to migrate to cloud infrastructure carries significant long-term security implications.

words.definition: Belonging naturally; essential to the core constitution of something.
words.example: Autonomous problem-solving is an intrinsic motivator for skilled creative professionals.

words.definition: The capacity to recover quickly from difficulties; toughness and adaptability.
words.example: The team demonstrated extraordinary resilience when pivoting the product under tight constraints.

words.definition: Performed or occurring as a result of a sudden natural impulse without premeditation.
words.example: The seminar concluded with a spontaneous round of applause from the attendees.

words.definition: So delicate or understated as to be difficult to perceive, yet carrying significant nuance.
words.example: A subtle shift in vocal intonation completely transformed the meaning of the spoken sentence.

words.definition: Perceptible by touch; clear, definite, and concrete rather than purely theoretical.
words.example: The customer onboarding redesign produced tangible improvements in user retention within weeks.
